title: cam stop must kill the sidecar + clean all markers; cam run abnormal-exit orphans the sidecar
description: Dogfood 2026-06-17: after the operator closed the session and ran cam stop, an orphan cam sidecar process was still running (observed ~11h uptime, having survived multiple sessions; sidecars accumulate, consistent with the 'two sidecars alive ~15h' seen in the CAM-56 dogfood), plus stale markers left behind (.claude/.cam-orch-session, .claude/.cam-worker-pane, scripts/cam/worker-report.json). cam stop kills the tmux session but does NOT kill the sidecar process and does not clean all markers; and a cam run killed abnormally (session closed rather than a clean SIGINT/SIGTERM to the cam run process) orphans its sidecar (the sidecar only dies via cam run's own SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup handler). Result: orphan sidecars poll forever and pile up across sessions. Fix: (1) cam stop locates and kills the project's sidecar (via the supervisor-lock recorded pid, or a scoped kill) and removes ALL per-session markers (.cam-orch-session, .cam-worker-pane, worker-report.json, .cam-supervisor.lock, cam-loop.local.md, .cam-orch-ready); (2) the sidecar self-terminates when its session is gone (poll for the tmux session and exit if absent within one idle interval) so an orphan can never poll indefinitely. Acceptance sketch: after cam stop, no cam sidecar process remains and all markers are gone; killing the cam run session without a clean stop leaves no orphan sidecar within one poll interval; a regression test on the cam stop teardown (lock-pid kill + marker cleanup) and on the sidecar session-absent self-exit. NOT CAM-58 (that is the loop false-terminal/outcome logic). Relates to the sidecar lifecycle (CAM-55 spawn, CAM-57 self-heal) and the memory note that active:false alone does not halt the sidecar. Source: dogfood observation.
